version: No version number in the skill. The last changelog entry is 2026-10-04 (Script Lab and Hook Lab wiring), which is before hub v13.3 (2026-10-08) and v13.4 (2026-10-11).
purpose: Builds a paid song ad from start to finish, "a sales letter set to music, not a jingle", sung by a person, character or object in a stylized look (Pixar-style 3D, clay, felt, yarn). The steps are: brand research, the Hook Lab (3 graded hook stacks with Nano Banana 2 concept frames), the argument written and gated as speech by Script Lab, then lyrics graded read flat. The user generates the song in Suno by hand. Then the skill re-times on the vocal stem (BPM, Whisper, UVR stem), plans shots with the 10 shot-logic tests, makes a style bible and Nano Banana 2 2K sheets, builds storyboards per sequence and renders lip-synced multi-shot clips on MiniMax H3 (reference mode with the vocal-stem slice). The edit is done in the Higgsfield sandbox, with a frame check, a cross-correlation sync check, 1080x1920 at 30 fps, captions, a hook super and an end card with the offer. There are 6 human GATEs. Appendix S holds 9 transcribed DTC song swipes (47 to 189 s) with beat maps.

phases.name: Preconditions: the Hook card and the Script Lab card
phases.does: Load readymerce-hook-lab and readymerce-script-lab with the Skill tool (if either fails to load, use its card and say so). Read Appendix S in full before every Phase 4. Read the Copy Laws (Appendix M, in Script Lab) before the first line of copy.
phases.gate: Hook bar: all 9 gates pass and every channel grades A or A+ (A+ 10, A 9, A- 8, B+ 7); an A- is rewritten. Script Lab: 16 mechanical tests plus a cold read and a 100-point score; release at 85 or more with no critical fail; up to 3 rewrite loops, then the user decides.
phases.tools_models: Skill tool; readymerce-hook-lab v1 card; readymerce-script-lab v1 card

phases.name: Inputs
phases.does: Ask for brand research (avatar doc, VOC, product truth, mechanism doc, offer) and the product URL. Read the avatars, VOC quotes, failed fixes and why each failed, the UMP and UMS, proof and reviews. Confirm the brand in one sentence plus 2 to 3 findings. One avatar per song.
phases.gate: The URL is the minimum. With neither research nor a URL, stop and ask.

phases.name: Genre and length
phases.does: Pick the genre from the demographic map (2 to 3 suggestions with reasons). Length follows the Script Lab router: an S60 or S90 story tier (55 to 100 s) as the first test plus a C45 short tier (40 to 50 s, the Penrose 47 s problem-rap model). L150 only with a stated reason. Aim at the tier's lower end because Suno runs 10 to 25 s long.
phases.gate: No story under 55 s. Both tiers are written, even if only the short tier is rendered.
phases.human_checkpoint: GATE 2: genre and the tiers (a story tier and a short tier)

phases.name: Angle and awareness
phases.does: One angle in customer language, one awareness stage with a reason, and THE PICTURE (the plain contrast that makes the cause obvious), named as the UMP. The chorus repeats that name.
phases.gate: Promise as strong and specific as the research allows.

phases.name: Hook Lab (H0 to H6, before any lyric)
phases.does: Check the category Hook Library (under 60 days old). Generate stacks: a visual shot spec, the text hook, the sung hook (lyric line 1 or 2) and the seam line. Song rules: problem on screen at 0 s, text hook held from frame 1, first sung word by about 1 s, problem sung by about 3 s, and the line passes the gates read flat. Keep 3 per format (a master and 2 variants, at least 2 hook types), each with a Nano Banana 2 concept frame (about 2 credits) checked at phone size with the text hook laid on top. A variant with a new sung line needs its own Suno opening (Replace Section).
phases.gate: All 9 Hook Lab gates, every channel A or A+. A stack that fails Script Lab test 12 (the seam) goes back to H6.
phases.human_checkpoint: Stacks shown and picked at GATE 4

phases.name: Swipe study and Script Lab WRITE (the argument as speech)
phases.does: Read Appendix S in full and pick the 2 closest swipe ads per spine (MODELED ON). Send Script Lab the brief card, the song format adapter (18b), the tiers, the hook stacks and the cast. It returns 2 or 3 spines of about 80 words. After the pick it returns the released speech script per tier: line table, pre-write pack, gate report and length ladder. Song moves menu: H, SC, FF, T, promise, M (chorus), D, ING, TL/PO, PR, OF, G, U, ID.
phases.gate: Script Lab gate (16 tests plus a cold read; 85/100 with no critical fail).

phases.name: Formats, lyric rules and the lyric gate
phases.does: Each spine uses a different 4c format. Lyrics keep every rung in order; 8 to 14 syllables a line; the chorus carries the picture and its name and repeats at least twice; the turn, named problem, guarantee and CTA are spoken; the brand is sung or spoken at least twice, first only after the product is shown; Suno-safe spellings; vocal tags. Lines per tier: 35 to 55 for 90 s, 23 to 37 for an S60, 18 to 27 for a C45. A Suno style prompt under 25 words that includes 'clear lead vocal, lyrics up front'.
phases.gate: 4f: Script Lab GRADE on the lyrics read flat (tests 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 12, 13) plus a fresh-agent cold read; tests 1, 6 and 16 checked against the speech script; master stack passes the 9 gates at A or A+; chorus repeats at least twice; spoken lines present; line count fits the tier; full selling strength; as specific as the 2 swipe models. Rewrite until every answer is yes.
phases.human_checkpoint: GATE 4: the user picks a spine and its master hook stack (plus 2 variants). The user then generates each song in Suno (and any variant openings), uploads to Higgsfield and sends share links. If told to run without stopping, Claude picks the spine, but Suno stays manual.
phases.tools_models: Suno (run by the user, by hand); Script Lab GRADE/FIX

phases.name: Get the song into a workable place
phases.does: Work in the Higgsfield sandbox (sandbox_exec), which can reach Higgsfield files and has ffmpeg, sox, python3 and faster-whisper. It is wiped about 10 s after each call, so chain the work and upload in one command. Resolve share links with curl -L. Publish with media_upload, a PUT with If-None-Match, then media_confirm.
phases.human_checkpoint: User must put the song on Higgsfield or send a Suno link

phases.name: Audio analysis (the timing backbone)
phases.does: librosa beat_track for BPM and the beat grid (snap every cut to a beat). Word-timed transcript (faster-whisper word_timestamps, or sherpa-onnx in overlapping windows). UVR MDX-Net vocal stem. Re-time on the stem (RMS above about -38 dB). Report the length, a slow hook, misheard words, changed lyrics and brand pronunciation. Trim the intro so the voice arrives within 0.3 s.
phases.gate: The stem sits about 30 dB below the mix in instrumental parts. Slow hook (more than 3 s before the first problem line): the user regenerates that opening in Suno before any visuals, and a slow hook never ships. A sung change that alters meaning goes back through Script Lab FIX (tests 3, 5 to 10, 13, 14, or the full gate for a core rung) and is re-sung with Replace Section.
phases.human_checkpoint: No numbered gate; the user regenerates openings or lines in Suno
phases.tools_models: librosa; faster-whisper (small.en/medium.en) or sherpa-onnx-whisper-small.en int8; UVR-MDX-NET-Voc_FT.onnx

phases.name: Visual plan and shot logic
phases.does: Show what is sung: every line gets its own picture, changing every 1.5 to 3.5 s. Group lines into sequences of 3 to 6 shots, each up to 15 s, that share one audio slice (2-minute song: 8 to 10 sequences; S90: 6 to 8; C45: 3 to 5). The hook shows the problem from frame 1 and the failed attempt by about 3 s. Write each shot as 'who does what to what, and what visibly changes'. Run the 10 shot-logic tests: one-second read; cause and visible result in the same shot; contrast, not stunt, for abstract lines; narrator asides set up the next idea; real-world logic; edit effects stay in the edit; one panel = one moment = one state per character; the prop that carries the line is exact; the thing that carries the line is the subject; a blocked or simplified shot must still carry its line. List the characters, states, props and settings.
phases.gate: Shot logic table (line | who does what | what visibly changes | what a stranger reads in 1 second | pass/fail). Only passing shots go to Phase 9.

phases.name: Style bible, character bible and sheets
phases.does: 8a: style block (9:16 for scenes), closing line, motion guard, a palette of 4 to 6 named colours, character rules (the product is never a character). 8b: a locked character bible pasted word for word into prompts. 8c sheets in order on Nano Banana 2 at 2K: hero sheet (16:9 or 1:1, four views plus three expressions), human sheet, group sheet, product sheet (label checked letter by letter), setting sheets, key prop sheet with the exact reading. 8d: state and variant sheets. 8e: optional Higgsfield reference elements (H3 does not read them). 8f: the reference flow table. 8g: consistency checks after every image and every clip.
phases.gate: Each sheet is checked at full size before the next. 8g: face, details and outfit match; body matches the sheet or state sheet; sidekicks keep size and order; label single and readable; no clones, nobody floats, props match. A character that drifts is retaken with its sheet moved earlier.
phases.human_checkpoint: GATE 5: the user approves every sheet before any storyboard or video

phases.name: Storyboard image per sequence
phases.does: One image holds every shot as panels: 3 shots on a 16:9 canvas of three 9:16 panels; 4 to 6 shots on a 4:5 canvas in a 2 x 3 grid. Thin white gutters, no text. References are the sheets, the setting, the prop sheet and the previous storyboard. Each panel is one frozen moment with people counted and exact prop readings. The hook storyboard is made and checked first.
phases.gate: Storyboard check: open at full size, fill the shot-logic row for every panel, and check clones, floating, props and subject size. Any fail means regenerate. Never send a storyboard to H3 that has not been looked at. The hook storyboard is checked at phone size with the text hook, sound off.
phases.human_checkpoint: GATE 6: the user approves the storyboards with the shot logic table, hook storyboard first
phases.tools_models: Image model not named in Phase 9 (sheets and concept frames are Nano Banana 2)

phases.name: Video generation (MiniMax H3 on Higgsfield)
phases.does: Reference mode (up to 9 images and up to 3 audio clips of 15 s max, no start or end frame) for every singing sequence. Keyframe mode (start frame, optional end frame, no references or audio) for non-singing shots. The two modes are never mixed. The audio reference is the vocal-only stem slice from the sequence's first frame, with a 0.03 s fade, padded to whole seconds; duration = the padded length. Tokens <<<image_1>>> and <<<audio_1>>> in upload order. The 7-part prompt: style block, references, timeline with one action per shot, transitions ('exactly N shots'), lip-sync block, camera, motion guard. Aspect 9:16 set explicitly. Batch 2 on singing and hook sequences. Fallbacks: split into 2 clips, then a keyframe render plus Sync Lipsync 3. An NSFW block means redesigning the shot. Budget preflight before rendering.
phases.gate: The cross-correlation of the clip audio with the reference should peak at 0 ms lag. Budget: price per second times seconds times takes, plus about 30% retakes, with the balance checked right before submitting.
phases.tools_models: MiniMax H3 (Higgsfield; no model id, resolution or declined_preset_id given); Sync Lipsync 3 (fallback)

phases.name: Deliverables before rendering
phases.does: Per sequence: a timing table (shot, seconds, lyric, what you see, one-second read), the storyboard prompt with its ordered refs, the video prompt with refs and audio, slices named SEQ_vocal_<start>-<end>_pad<N>s.mp3 plus fallback splits, and the edit placement. All of it saved in the project doc with the style and character bibles and the sheet ID table.

phases.name: Edit and assembly (Higgsfield sandbox)
phases.does: Find renders with show_generations and download them. Mandatory frame check: one middle frame per shot on contact sheets. Sync check by cross-correlation; trim with faster-whisper if the lag is not 0. Normalize to 1080x1920 at 30 fps (crop square clips to 810x1440 by motion). Fit clips with trim or setpts speed-ups up to about 2.7x. Concat in song order over the master song from the trim point, with clip audio muted and a 1 s fade at the end. Edit effects are added here. Captions are the words as sung, 1 to 3 per card. Then the hook super, other supers, an end card with the CTA, offer, guarantee and fine print, the upload, and a 9:16 export (4:5 if asked).
phases.gate: Frame check: run the 7a tests and 8g checks on every frame, list failing shots with fixes, and retake before the final edit. If frames can't be viewed, say so plainly. Caption safe zone: top 14% and bottom 20% clear.
phases.human_checkpoint: The user sees the list of failing shots
phases.tools_models: ffmpeg, faster-whisper medium.en plus difflib alignment; Higgsfield show_generations, media_upload, media_confirm

phases.name: QA and policy
phases.does: Sound-off watch (do the supers tell the story; one-second read per shot). Hook check on the first 3 s at phone size, sound off, then sound on (first sung word by about 1 s, problem by about 3 s). Sheets match (8g); lip-sync stays on its picture; product shown before its name; no generated text; Meta ad review risk on an exaggerated before-and-after (keep a fallback hook with a normal figure); watch at phone size.
phases.gate: Any shot that looks pretty but means nothing is replaced.
phases.human_checkpoint: The user decides on the Meta fallback hook

claims.quote: ### 8c. Sheet types and prompt templates (Nano Banana 2, 2K)
claims.note: Song part confirmed: sheets use Nano Banana 2 at 2K (L272), and concept frames use Nano Banana 2 at about 2 credits each (L105). Caveat: Phase 9 storyboards name no image model or resolution; Nano Banana 2 for storyboards is only implied (8e lists it among models that read elements). Cross-check in the hub (readymerce-ads-machine L109): 'Realistic people: GPT Image 2 (`gpt_image_2`, quality high, 2k)' and 'GPT Image 2.5 smoothed the skin into a plastic look'. The hub also says 'Stylized work keeps the style skill's model', so Nano Banana 2 in the song skill does not break the hub. Podcast and carousel were not checked here.

claims.quote: padded with silence to a whole number of seconds. Render duration = that padded length.
claims.note: The song skill uses '= padded slice'. Drama confirms the other side (readymerce-drama-ads L542: 'Generate the H3 clip at the stem length plus 1 s. An H3 job whose duration equals the audio length fails'). Risk in the song rule: no +1 s margin and no 5 s floor, so a slice that already ends on a whole second renders at exactly the audio length, the case drama says fails.

claims.quote: of 3 to 6 shots, each up to 15 seconds (H3's limit)
claims.note: The song's own lessons log (L395) hedges: 'H3 handles 3 shots per take reliably; 6 is possible but keep the split fallback ready.' Animation L549 says '2 to 3 shots per take reliably; 4 is possible'. The hub G1 card (ads-machine L90) says '2 to 4 shots per clip'. Internal tension: a 15 s sequence of 3 shots gives 5 s per picture, which breaks the skill's own 1.5 to 3.5 s cadence (L211).

story_structures.name: Named-person story: one person, three tiny scenes
story_structures.shape: H name + age or role -> SC1, SC2, SC3 (tiny concrete scenes with times, places, objects) -> FF shelf of failed fixes, each killed with WHY -> T 'Here's what nobody told X' + the cause in one plain line, named -> M chorus teaches the picture and repeats its name -> D the fix shown before it is named -> TL 'three weeks in' -> PO scene 3 reversed exactly -> ID close
story_structures.organic_fit: The closest match to 'POV, a day in the buyer's life, then the mechanism revealed'. Example: 'This is Erion, he runs a dental clinic in Durres': filming a reel at 11 pm, 4 likes, an unanswered DM at lunch, a boosted post that brought likes and no bookings. Failed fixes (posting daily, the nephew, boosting) each get a reason. The chorus names the picture (for example, the shop window with nobody at the till). The payoff reverses scene 1: the phone buzzes with a booked consult. Close on identity plus a spoken organic CTA ('Comment SISTEM and we'll send the 3 steps' / 'Send this to an owner who needs it'). Runs S60 (55 to 65 s); no price, offer or guarantee. Strongest default for a story post.

story_structures.name: Confession (first person), with a count or an honest dip
story_structures.shape: H bold result others noticed, or an admission with a number -> FF precise failures ('orange by noon, cakey by 3pm') -> SC low point ('maybe this is just my age') -> D + objection killed -> demo/PO -> M reframe chorus that removes blame ('It was never the skin, it was never the age') -> count payoff + name ('47 tries... 48 was the one'); RYZE variant: TL day 1 nothing, 'you kind of feel scammed', then early results
story_structures.organic_fit: An owner's or founder's first-person song: 'I posted 300 times last year and got 4 clients.' The reframe chorus ('It was never the posting, it was never the algorithm') removes blame, which fits organic well and earns comments and shares. The count payoff and the honest dip (week 1 nothing) build trust. Needs a real person and real numbers (facts list). CTA: follow for part 2, or a comment keyword.

story_structures.name: Antagonist story
story_structures.shape: H age + confession -> SC antagonist + deadline -> FF + why -> D a friend brings the fix + objection -> demo -> M vs the failed fixes -> ING -> PO social win (the antagonist asks 'what's that?') -> callback to the hook -> late brand reveal -> ID
story_structures.organic_fit: A rival business across the street that is always booked, a deadline (the slow season, a launch), and a friend who shows the method. The payoff is the rival asking 'who does your content?'. It is quotable, comic and earns sends. Never name a real competitor. The brand is said at most once, late (or only on the handle). CTA: comment keyword.

story_structures.name: Characters explain: each part sings its own job
story_structures.shape: H conditional ('If a X took this...') -> each character walks on and sings one job paired with one visible symptom -> PO social ('friends ask...') -> PR -> U + CTA calling back the hook's person
story_structures.organic_fit: Recurring characters for a series. The culprits (the boosted post, the unanswered DM, the dead 'link in bio') or the method's parts (Hook, Script, Funnel, Follow-up) each sing one job tied to one visible business symptom. Save-worthy, because it teaches the system. The skill's 'the product is never a character' rule is about physical products, so for a service the steps can be characters. CTA: 'Save this so you remember the 4 jobs' or a comment keyword.

story_structures.name: Two futures / 'if you took this'
story_structures.shape: H two futures ('the difference between... is one easy thing') -> SC told as the two futures -> T the one thing -> FF + why x2 -> M a picture (the dam) -> ING 'if you did X, it would...' -> PR -> routine + brand -> vs the failed fixes -> PO -> OF + G + U
story_structures.organic_fit: 'The difference between a salon that posts and prays and one whose DMs book themselves is one thing.' Each 'if you did step N, it would...' line teaches one move. Drop OF, G and U urgency and end on save or follow. Makes the viewer pick a side, which drives comments.

story_structures.name: Fable
story_structures.shape: H 'Once was a soul who...' -> FF x2 -> T wrong cause (blame the tools, not the person) -> D -> each function as a visible action -> PO -> ID 'you're not broken, you never once were'
story_structures.organic_fit: 'Once was a baker in Tirana who posted every dawn...' A gentle, shareable, blame-free story with a stylized mascot (felt or clay, one material). The skill rates it a story, so S60 or longer. The identity close is ideal for organic. CTA: follow, or send to a friend.

story_structures.name: Problem rap (the natural C45 short tier)
story_structures.shape: H problem in their words -> promise ('what if one thing...') -> FF + why in one line of everyday physics -> M one plain line -> the fix keeps the current habit -> PO social -> price anchor vs money already spent -> OF -> brand + promise -> U + ID
story_structures.organic_fit: The cheapest song format (C45 is 3 to 5 sequences). 'Your page looks fire but your DMs are dead by noon.' One-line cause, then 'keep posting what you post, add one thing'. Replace the price anchor with a time anchor (hours already spent filming) and drop the offer. Spoken CTA with a comment keyword. Best default for a first organic song test or a hook-plus-chorus cut.

story_structures.name: Transformation timeline (result + timeframe, honest dip)
story_structures.shape: H result + timeframe ('hid X for 15 years... here's what happened after 30 days') -> TL first days / weeks / day 30, each part's job in time order -> FF killed in one line ('unlike creams on the surface') -> PO -> U -> OF -> ID
story_structures.organic_fit: A real client case study as a song: day 1, week 1 (nothing yet, the honest dip), day 30 (the calendar fills). Only with a real client's permission and real numbers from the facts list. CTA: 'Follow to see day 60' (a series hook).

story_structures.name: The song moves menu (beat codes mapped to the belief ladder)
story_structures.shape: H (rung 0-1) -> SC (1-2) -> FF (3) -> T (4) -> promise (5) -> M taught in the chorus (6) -> D + ING (7) -> TL + PO + PR (8) -> OF, G, U (9-12) -> ID (13)
story_structures.organic_fit: Keep H through PR and ID. Replace rungs 9 to 12 (offer, guarantee, urgency, 'link below') with one organic spoken CTA. PR only as real social proof (client count or reviews as shown). The tier still decides how many moves fit.

story_structures.name: Visual treatments from the swipe file
story_structures.shape: Draw the claim on the body or object -> competitor products rendered playfully in yarn or clay -> genre or style switch where viewers usually drop -> one material for the whole ad -> a counter that climbs with the lyrics -> ingredients walk on as characters -> callbacks (an early object returns) -> flashback for 'like you used to'
story_structures.organic_fit: Series look for an agency account: one material (felt or clay) used every month so the brand is recognized; a climbing counter (posts made, DMs missed, hours spent); a genre switch at the mechanism verse to hold retention; competitors' tactics shown playfully (never real names). These work unchanged for organic.

organic_adaptation: Close: replace rungs 9 to 12 (OF offer, G guarantee, U urgency and 'link below') and the Phase 12.9 end card ('CTA, the offer exactly as the page shows it, the guarantee, and the fine print') with one spoken organic CTA tied to the hub keyword funnel (comment KEYWORD, save, send to a friend, follow for part 2). No price, price anchor, guarantee or scarcity. Keep lyric rule 7 (the CTA is a spoken line so it can't be misheard).

Script Lab gate: its 12 rules include 'offer before the CTA' and the 100-point score expects offer and CTA rungs. Add an organic format adapter (or a song-organic variant of 18b) so a missing offer is not scored as a missing rung.

Length: the skill's first test is S60/S90 (55 to 100 s), 'No story under 55 s', and Suno adds 10 to 25 s. For organic, default to the C45 problem rap (40 to 50 s, 3 to 5 sequences) or a hook-plus-chorus cut of about 20 to 35 s. Keep S60 for series episodes. Add a sub-C45 row to the lines-per-tier rule (4d.11). Trim Suno intros and outros harder.

Hook rules: keep the 9 gates and 'no product, brand, mechanism name, price or offer in the first 3 s'. Replace the DTC-health parts ('where it lives on the body', 'in a cartoon, one real-looking body part', 'no "your [condition]" or age label', 'never medical severity', the before-and-after Meta check) with a B2B/services profile: the problem where it lives in the business (an empty DM inbox, an unbooked calendar, a phone face down, a post with 4 likes), the owner annoyed, never ashamed.

Metrics and learning: the live read is paid only (about 1,000 impressions per stack, hook rate, hold rate, CTR, 'Cost per purchase at ad-set level decides'). Replace with organic Insights: 3-second hold and skip rate, average watch time and completion, sends per reach, saves, follows per reach, keyword comments and funnel DMs, non-follower reach. 3 stacks per post can't be split-tested organically, so use Instagram Trial Reels or run the variants on different days. LEARN must read organic data.

Compliance and claims: 'Write at full selling strength... the brand's legal team reviews every script' does not apply to an agency's organic post (there is no legal team). Keep 'Facts stay real', and allow only real, permitted client results. Drop the 'Results vary'/FDA fine print and the Phase 13.6 Meta ad review fallback. Check Instagram community guidelines instead.

AI label: the skill has none. Add the shared rule (Instagram 'AI info' label for AI-generated characters and scenes, including stylized 3D, clay or felt) and a matching caption line if the house standard requires it.

Product reveal timing: the rules 'product shown before its name' and 'Brand name sung or spoken at least twice' are hard-sell for organic. The 'product' is the agency's method. Name the method (the UMP picture) in the chorus, say the brand at most once (end card or handle), turn discovery (D) into 'how the owner found the fix', and teach enough of the mechanism that the post is useful without buying (save-worthy).

Song generation: GATE 4 makes the user generate each song in Suno by hand, which blocks an automated weekly pipeline. Add an ElevenLabs Music route (eleven_music_v2_5 with lyrics, 2 to 3 takes, picked by a Whisper match to the lyrics) as an option, keep Suno as the alternative (the hub currently says 'Song ads keep Suno'), and keep a human listen gate before any video.

Language: lyrics in Albanian need the Suno-safe spelling rule extended (numbers as words, brand phonetics, the hub's G8 Albanian negation lesson 'nuk' vs 's''), and a word-by-word Whisper check of the sung lyrics. Captions in Albanian. The genre map has no Albanian or B2B-owner rows.

Swipe file: Appendix S is 9 US DTC consumer songs (supplements, skincare, cologne). Organic B2B needs its own reference set (refbank cards) with the same beat maps, and the 'MODELED ON' step should point there.

Human gates and cost: 6 numbered gates plus a manual Suno step is too heavy for a weekly organic cadence. Batch them into one approval queue (spine+hook, song listen, sheets, storyboards, final). Build the world once (style bible, character and prop sheets saved as Higgsfield elements, 8e) and run songs as a monthly series to reuse sheets.

Cover and caption: organic needs a cover frame (the text hook doubles as the reel title or cover) plus the post caption with the keyword; the skill delivers only the video. Send it to hub.py as a draft.
Exports and safe zones: keep 9:16 at 1080x1920. Unify caption and CTA safe zones with the shared standard (the song uses top 14% and bottom 20%; drama uses bottom 35 to 40% for Reels UI).
visual_qa_overlap: What the skill already does: (1) Concept frames per hook stack are checked at phone size with the text hook laid on top (3b.5). (2) The 10 shot-logic tests in Phase 7a run as a written table before any image (line | who does what | what visibly changes | 1-second read | pass/fail). (3) Sheets: each is checked at full size before the next; the product label is checked letter by letter; the 8g consistency checks run after every image and clip (face, details, outfit, body vs sheet or state sheet, sidekick size and order, single readable label, no clones, nobody floating, props match their reading); a drifting character is retaken with its sheet moved earlier; human GATE 5. (4) Storyboard check after every storyboard: every panel at full size, the shot-logic row filled, counts and clones, floating, impossible poses, props with a reason and matching the prop sheet, subject big enough at phone size. The hook storyboard is first, at phone size with the text hook, sound off, keeping the concept frame's subject and scale. Human GATE 6. (5) Prompts: a fixed 7-part H3 reference-mode structure, the motion guard and closing line, one action per shot, people counted, no edit effects in prompts (7a.6), one state per character (7a.7), exact prop readings (7a.8), and NSFW rewrites re-run through tests 1 to 9. There is NO prompt review step: the same agent writes and approves prompts. (6) Takes: Phase 12.2 grabs ONE frame from the middle of every shot at about 180x320, WebP q40, 6 to 8 clips per sheet, and runs the 7a and 8g tests; sync is a single cross-correlation; Phase 13 checks sound-off, the hook, sheet match, lip-sync on picture, product before name, no generated text. A fresh-agent Visual/Prompt/Take Reviewer would REPLACE self-review with an independent cold check: test 1 literally asks for 'a stranger', but today the author of the shot judges it (Script Lab already does this for words with its cold read). It would ADD: (a) a Prompt Reviewer that lints every storyboard and H3 prompt before spend against the hub G1 card (reference tokens in upload order, hands and props line, background-action line, one action per shot, the 'exactly N shots' transition line, the lip-sync block with pause list, negatives) and the job parameters the song skill lacks (minimax_h3, resolution 2K, aspect 9:16, declined_preset_id, duration of at least 5 s and longer than the audio); (b) a Visual Reviewer for sheets and storyboards that sees only the shot spec plus the image and scores the one-second read, counts and clones, and the prop reading and label, with full-resolution crops (growth-engine/tools/vqa_crops.py exists) instead of a 180x320 thumbnail; (c) a Take Reviewer that samples several frames per shot (first, middle, last, plus every cut) rather than one mid-frame, so it catches mid-shot morphs, clones, vanishing props and generated text; checks the mouth of the singer against the stem; runs the hub G6 windowed drift check (2 s windows every 0.25 s) instead of a single lag; and transcribes the re-sung audio against the lyrics; (d) a Failure Library seeded from the skill's lessons log (the Pillow Pool slop list: two Danas from 'sits up, groans and flops back', the wrong digital clock, the floating 'frozen mid-flop', the duvet spotlight after the NSFW rewrite); (e) logged pass/fail per shot so GATE 5 and 6 humans see a pre-screened set.

There is no Suno tool and no ElevenLabs Music route; the hub (ads-machine L122) still says 'Song ads keep Suno'. An automated agent stalls at GATE 4 and again in Phase 6.

Missing H3 job parameters versus hub G1 v13.3: no model id (`minimax_h3`), no `resolution: "2K"`, no `declined_preset_id` (the hub says that without it 'the API recommends a preset instead of submitting the job'), and no 5 s minimum (hub: 'a 4-second render failed in testing').
